THE CROSS-FLAGSHIP VERIFICATION CONTRACT F151 may pass traceable batch identity, robot operation timing and status of independent qualification to F152, but it may not pass a presumed biological quality claim. F152 may share physical sensor status and external fault labels with F153, but a low alarm count is not permission to run the next experiment. F153 may propose new tests while an authorized human panel retains control of approval and veto. F154 receives only commands within its pre-authorized local hardware envelope; independent emergency-stop circuits cannot be overridden by an AI policy. F155 receives the typed protocol, calibration provenance and failed execution records, and tests whether another vendor device produces equivalent physical actions without privileged tuning. Every inter-flagship signal carries its unit, confidence bounds, timestamp, data lineage, authority and invalidity conditions. The thirty candidate mathematical relations in the PDF include accounting identities, sensor-performance ratios, timing budgets, review queue measures, dimensionless transfer loss and uncertainty-sensitive reproducibility scores. Each states its assumptions and dimensions. The forty-two three-dimensional models are explicitly synthetic and independently recalculable from raw numerical formulas and stored CSV triples. They are visualization and software-reconstruction exercises, not material validation. The eighty-two research chapters repeat a six-phase logic with different physical questions: physical identity and authorization, fair competing explanation, recomputed three-dimensional sensitivity, blinded independent measurement, benign counterfactual fault challenge, external transfer and permission to refuse. Their three literary and scientific voices are mechanism, measurement and refutation. A reader should find genuine scientific disagreement and a feasible negative answer, not merely an impressive number of pages. The two hundred Research Gates are planned future investigations with a distinct origin, an extreme counterworld and an independent research plan. They do not promise that robotic laboratories will be more accurate, biological samples more mature or quantum and AI computations magically faster than physical constraints permit. The thirty-three Phoenix prototypes are nonclinical and predominantly inert apparatus concepts: batch-accounting ledgers, blind sensor fault chambers, human veto interfaces, safe-state clocks and cross-device reference artifacts. Their purpose is to be built, modified, contradicted or retired by future engineers. An honest boundary is a durable scientific inheritance. A CROSS-FLAGSHIP EXPERIMENTAL CONTRACT The five flagships can share a disciplined interface without sharing a causal conclusion. F146 transmits mechanically calibrated geometry and force bounds, never a presumed cell phenotype. F147 transmits flux and concentration ranges with a complete solute ledger. F148 transmits synchronized electrical and strain signals, including the electrode artifact reference. F149 transmits temperature and metered heat flows, distinguishing thermal blank from putative metabolism. F150 receives sensitivities, covariances and data provenance, then asks whether the combined physical parameter vector is actually identifiable. Failure of that inverse problem forces the other flagships to narrow claims about which coefficients were learned. Even if a model makes an accurate prediction, several mechanisms may remain observationally equivalent. The thirty candidate mathematical relations are hypotheses under declared domains. Elastic strain and traction use consistent stress and displacement units. Reaction, diffusion and advection obey a source-and-flux convention with integral conservation. Bioelectric fields, current density and hypothetical electromechanical strain carry different dimensions. Heat capacity, conductivity, perfusion and volumetric source terms must close an energy equation. Sensitivity and Fisher information depend on parameter scaling and measurement covariance. None of these established mathematical forms validates an unmeasured coupling coefficient. The forty-two three-dimensional examples are designed as audit exercises so an external reviewer can reproduce each vertex and inspect unstable edges. The two hundred Research Gates are not endpoints achieved; they are independently stated invitations. Every Gate poses an origin problem, an extreme counterworld able to counterfeit success, and a future action with an external witness and explicit stop. The thirty-three Phoenix concepts remain inert, nonclinical apparatus proposals until an authorized experimental program builds and tests them. Their value is not that they foretell a technological triumph. It is that they make the next falsifiable physical question easier to ask, reproduce and refine.
